Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are David Larson, Chief Executive Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer; and Thomas Berger, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Larson.

David Larson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our strong performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key aspects: total admissions and patient days year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year; same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year; and capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion.

These metrics highlight the resilience of our operations across our network of 85 acute care hospitals and 22 freestanding emergency rooms in 14 states, primarily in the Southeast, Midwest, and Southwest. We saw robust volume growth driven by surgical services, high-acuity cases, and effective use of technology. Our teams have optimized capacity and payer relationships to support this momentum, while investing thoughtfully in expansions that position us for the future.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Robert Hayes to provide a more detailed review of our financial results and expand on these areas.

Robert Hayes:
Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $2.58 billion, an increase of 6.5% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved payer mix, and continued strength in high-margin service lines.

Our operating expenses were $2.10 billion, representing 81.4% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization through our proprietary consortium.

Net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.18 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me now dive deeper into the key aspects David highlighted, starting with our core volume metrics—total admissions and patient days—which continue to underscore the strength of our operational execution amid a dynamic healthcare landscape. These metrics are unadjusted for outpatient equivalents and reflect activity across our full network.

In the second quarter, we delivered 162,300 total admissions, representing 8.2% year-over-year growth from 150,000 in Q2 2023, and 2.5% sequential growth from 158,200 in Q1 2024. On patient days, we achieved 1.081 million days, up 8.0% year-over-year from 1.001 million in the prior-year quarter and up 3.0% quarter-over-quarter from 1.049 million in Q1. This translated to an average length of stay—or ALOS—of 6.66 days, stable sequentially but up 20 basis points year-over-year, driven by a modest uptick in high-acuity medical cases.

Year-over-year admissions growth was broad-based. Surgical services, which account for 42% of our mix, surged 11.5% to 68,200 admissions. Elective volumes—like orthopedics, cardiology, and neurosurgery—jumped 14%, fueled by pent-up demand and our expanded capacity from last year's $250 million bed expansion program. For context, our hip and knee replacement volumes are now running 20% above pre-pandemic levels, aligning with national trends reported by the American Hospital Association.

Medical admissions grew 6.8% year-over-year to 72,100, with strength in cardiovascular up 9% and pulmonology up 7%, partly due to seasonal respiratory illnesses and the ongoing GLP-1 wave—think Ozempic and Mounjaro—boosting related endocrine admissions by 12%, though partially offset by fewer bariatric procedures. Behavioral health, 12% of our mix, rose 5% to 15,400 admissions, benefiting from our partnership with Teladoc Health for virtual crisis triage, which improved access and reduced no-show rates by 15%. Other categories, including oncology and maternity, were up 4% overall.

Sequentially, the 2.5% quarter-over-quarter admissions lift came despite typical seasonality, with surgical volumes up 4% on stronger case mix—our CMI, or case mix index, expanded 1.2% quarter-over-quarter to 1.68—and medical admissions flat as flu activity normalized post-Q1 peak.

On patient days, the year-over-year story mirrors admissions but with ALOS tailwinds: our adjusted patient days—factoring in a 1.2x outpatient multiplier—grew 9.1% to 1.95 million, outpacing raw days due to robust observation and outpatient surge capacity utilization at 92%. Average daily census, or ADC, hit 11,900 beds, up 7.5% year-over-year and reflecting 85% overall occupancy, with flagship markets like Atlanta and Dallas exceeding 90%.

Regionally, performance was strongest in the Southeast, where admissions grew 10.3% year-over-year—led by our Florida and Georgia clusters amid robust commercial payer mix at 58% of revenues and favorable Medicare Advantage penetration. The Midwest saw 7.1% growth, tempered by reimbursement pressures from Blue Cross Blue Shield contract renegotiations, while the Southwest delivered 6.8%, with Texas ER-driven admissions offsetting rural capacity constraints. Notably, our de novo freestanding ER in Phoenix contributed 1,200 incremental admissions, validating our micro-hospital strategy in high-growth Sun Belt markets.

Powering this are several technical initiatives yielding tangible results: Epic MyChart optimization post our system-wide go-live in Q4 2023 has improved patient throughput by 12%, with digital pre-arrival check-ins reducing admission delays by 25 minutes on average, directly boosting same-day surgical slots. AI-driven capacity management, leveraging predictive analytics from Cerner and our proprietary RevOps platform, has optimized bed turnover by 18%, turning 1.2 extra beds per hospital into $15 million of incremental EBITDA. Value-based care ramp, with 35% of our Medicare lives now under ACO REACH or bundled payments, is driving 5% higher acuity shifts without proportional ALOS extension, as evidenced by our 2% CMI expansion year-over-year.

Strategically, these volumes affirm our focus on high-margin, high-acuity growth, prioritizing service line excellence—doubling down on transplant programs, where liver and kidney cases grew 22% year-over-year—and geographic densification, with three new hospitals under construction in Charlotte, Nashville, and Austin, adding 450 beds by 2026. Looking ahead, we expect Q3 admissions growth of 7-9% year-over-year, supported by back-to-school respiratory trends and elective catch-up, though mindful of potential CMS IPPS cuts and labor cost normalization. We remain confident in our ability to outperform peers like HCA and Community Health Systems, where our 8%+ volume CAGR positions us for sustained margin expansion.

Shifting to same-facility admissions and patient day growth, which provide a clean view of organic performance in our mature assets, excluding new facilities, divestitures, and major expansions. Same-facility admissions grew 2.4% year-over-year in Q2, accelerating from 1.8% in Q1 and marking our strongest quarterly print since Q4 2022. This came on the heels of a 3.1% quarter-over-quarter increase from Q1, driven by a robust rebound in elective procedures and high-acuity inpatient volumes. Patient days followed suit, up 1.9% year-over-year—slightly trailing admissions due to ongoing optimization in ALOS, which ticked down 0.4% to 4.7 days. Quarter-over-quarter, patient days rose 2.6%, reflecting stickier high-acuity cases amid seasonal respiratory pressures.

High-acuity admissions—think cardiac, neuro, and oncology—surged 4.2% year-over-year, comprising 28% of total admissions, up from 26% a year ago. This reflects our strategic emphasis on complex cases, with CMI expanding 1.6% to 1.82, bolstered by procedures like TAVR and CAR-T infusions. Lower-acuity ortho and general surgery admissions grew a more modest 1.1% year-over-year, but still marked a sequential improvement from flat in Q1. Patient days in high-acuity lines jumped 3.5% year-over-year, partially offset by a 2% year-over-year decline in observation-adjusted days as we push more cases to our ambulatory surgery centers, now numbering over 50 across our network.

Regionally, our Southeast cluster—45 hospitals from Florida to the Carolinas—led with 3.7% year-over-year admissions growth, fueled by pent-up demand in high Medicare density markets like Miami-Dade and Charlotte. Patient days expanded 2.8% year-over-year, with ALOS stable at 4.8 days despite flu season upticks. The Midwest, representing 30% of our beds, saw 1.9% year-over-year admissions growth but softer 0.7% patient day growth due to payer mix headwinds from Medicare Advantage denials, echoing challenges faced by peers like HCA and UHS. Urban markets like Chicago and Denver outperformed rural peers by 150 basis points on admissions, thanks to our density advantages and partnerships with systems like Cleveland Clinic for neuro referrals. West Coast facilities lagged at 0.8% year-over-year admissions growth amid California seismic retrofit costs and labor strikes, but we're mitigating with capacity reallocations from underutilized COVID surge units.

Driving this are volume tailwinds from deferred care catch-up: elective admissions are now running 15% above pre-pandemic levels, per CMS data, and our capture rate improved 200 basis points year-over-year via targeted direct-to-consumer campaigns on platforms like Healthgrades. Our enterprise-wide rollout of Epic MyChart with AI-driven predictive analytics—live in 85% of facilities—has reduced no-show rates by 12% and optimized bed turnover, contributing 40 basis points to admissions growth. Virtual nursing hubs, modeled after Cleveland Clinic's command centers, have boosted nurse-to-patient ratios in high-demand units and helped stabilize ALOS. Staffing remains tight, with RN vacancy rates at 8% network-wide, down from 12% year-over-year, supported by our $20 minimum wage tier and partnerships with Incredible Health for locums.

Strategically, we're idling 500 low-acuity beds in Q2 to prioritize CMI expansion, mirroring Tenet’s playbook, while investing $250 million in 2024 capex for 1,000 high-acuity beds and 20 new ASCs. Payer negotiations are key: our FY24 Medicare IPPS update, with its 2.9% bump for high-CMI hospitals, should accrete 50 basis points to net revenue per admission. For Q3, we guide same-facility admissions growth of 2.0-2.5% year-over-year and patient days of 1.5-2.0%, with upside from seasonal ortho volumes but risks from MA scrutiny and RSV surges. Risks like rising bad debt from Medicaid redeterminations are front-of-mind, but our 3.2% net revenue per patient day growth underscores pricing discipline.

Now, turning to capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, which remain a cornerstone of our long-term strategy to drive organic growth, enhance operational efficiency, and position us as a leader in value-based care across our network. For fiscal 2023, we deployed $452 million in CapEx, representing approximately 4.2% of our trailing twelve-month revenue and a 14% increase year-over-year from $397 million in 2022. This uptick reflects our disciplined acceleration of investments amid stabilizing reimbursement dynamics and robust patient volumes, with inpatient admissions up 7% and outpatient encounters surging 12% amid the ongoing shift to ambulatory care. In Q4 alone, we committed $118 million, in line with our guidance.

Roughly 62% or $280 million was allocated to facility modernization—up from 55% last year—prioritizing upgrades to boost clinical outcomes, reduce length of stay, and improve our case mix index. Key projects included the full rollout of Epic MyChart 2023 across 28 facilities, enhancing interoperability with payer portals and enabling AI-driven predictive analytics for readmission risk, which we expect to yield a 15-20 basis point lift in our Medicare Star ratings next year. We also invested $65 million in advanced diagnostic imaging, installing 12 new 3T Siemens Magnetom Vida MRI systems and eight GE Revolution Apex CT scanners optimized for low-dose cardiac imaging. These upgrades have already driven a 22% increase in high-margin neuroimaging volumes in pilot sites.

On expansion, we allocated $172 million, or 38% of total CapEx, focusing on high-ROI greenfield and brownfield developments. Standouts include the 120-bed tower addition at our flagship Miami-Dade Medical Center in Southeast Florida, addressing explosive population growth—up 2.8% annually per Census data—and competition from HCA Healthcare's recent $300 million Coral Gables expansion. This project, on track for Q3 2024 opening, incorporates 16 hybrid ORs equipped with Intuitive Surgical da Vinci Xi robots, targeting orthopedics and minimally invasive gyn procedures, segments where our CMI exceeds 1.85. We've also broken ground on three micro-hospitals in the Sun Belt—two in Texas suburbs near Dallas and one in Phoenix—totaling 75 beds at a blended cost of $12 million per facility. These freestanding EDs with observation units mirror Tenet Healthcare's successful model, ramping to 80-85% utilization within 12-18 months based on our Nashville prototype.

Regionally, spend skewed heavily toward the Southeast and Southwest, accounting for 55% of 2023 CapEx at $249 million. Florida and Texas hospitals saw $140 million deployed, capitalizing on Medicare Advantage penetration now at 42% in our markets—above the national 38% per CMS data—and demographic tailwinds from retirees and migrants. Midwest facilities received $85 million, primarily for HVAC retrofits to meet enhanced infection control standards post-COVID, including HEPA filtration systems that reduced HAIs by 18% in renovated ICUs. This regional mix aligns with our portfolio optimization, where Sun Belt assets now generate 62% of EBITDA despite comprising 48% of beds.

These investments focus on technology-enabled care, sustainability, and capacity for high-acuity services. We've embedded ESG priorities, with 40% of modernization CapEx toward LEED Silver certifications, including solar microgrids at five California hospitals to hedge against PG&E volatility and cut energy costs by 25%. Automation via robotics and ambient scribes is addressing nurse staffing pressures—our RN-to-patient ratio improved 8% post-upgrades—while positioning us for bundled payment models under CMS's upcoming GJRA rules.

Looking ahead, we're guiding to $485-510 million in CapEx for 2024, a 10% midpoint increase, with 65% weighted to modernization amid softening construction costs down 5-7% per Turner Building Cost Index. Payback periods average 3.5 years across the portfolio, with expansions projected to add $75 million in incremental EBITDA by 2026 at 2.5-3x multiples. This disciplined approach ensures we outperform peers like Community Health Systems, whose CapEx intensity lags at 3.5% of revenue, while maintaining our net leverage at 3.1x.

Finally, let's discuss our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and full year, as well as same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance. As we wrap up a solid first half, with adjusted EBITDA of $475 million on Q2 revenue—up 6.2% year-over-year—our focus remains on driving sustainable growth amid robust demand for elective procedures, labor optimization, and accelerating value-based care adoption. We've seen inpatient admissions rise 4.1% year-over-year to strong levels, with surgical volumes up 7.8%, fueled by a 12% rebound in orthopedics and cardiology cases post-COVID pent-up demand.

Priority one is organic growth and capacity expansion. We're prioritizing high-margin service lines in core markets. In the Sunbelt—where we operate 65% of our footprint—we expect same-facility revenue growth of 6-8% for the year, driven by a 5% increase in ALOS efficiency and expanded outpatient capacity. Our new ASCs in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro added meaningful revenue, with utilization at 82%, ahead of target. Nationally, we're on track to open three greenfield hospitals and convert five LTACHs to acute care by Q4, targeting 15,000 incremental licensed beds. This positions us to capture the aging demographic tailwind—CMS projects Medicare inpatient spending to grow 5.5% annually through 2030—while mitigating urban headwinds in the Northeast.

Priority two is margin expansion through operational excellence. Amid 4-6% medical supply inflation and RN wage pressures, we've achieved a 150-basis-point improvement in hospital cost per case mix-adjusted discharge, now at $12,450, via our supply chain consortium—saving $120 million annualized through bulk procurement of stents and joint implants from partners like Medtronic and Stryker. Labor optimization, post a 22% reduction in contract RNs through Cerner-integrated float pools and travel nurse caps, projects full-year labor costs at 52% of revenue, down from 54%. EBITDA margins hit 18.4% in Q2, guiding to 19-20% for FY24.

Priority three is digital transformation. Our $250 million tech roadmap has 85% of facilities live on Epic MyChart, boosting patient throughput by 11% and reducing no-show rates to under 8%. Telehealth volumes reached 18% of visits, up from 12% year-over-year, particularly in rural Midwest markets partnering with Teladoc. By year-end, we'll deploy AI-driven predictive analytics from Nuance and Google Cloud in 40 hospitals, targeting 15-20% readmission reduction via early sepsis detection. Cybersecurity follows ISO 27001 certification post-Change Healthcare breach lessons.

Priority four is payer and regulatory navigation. With commercial managed care at 55% of payer mix, we're deepening risk-sharing contracts—piloting bundled payments for MS-DRGs 470/471 in Florida, yielding 250 bps better margins. Medicare Advantage is at 28% of lives, countered by denials management tech from Waystar, recovering $35 million in Q1 underpayments. Tailwinds include 2.9% Medicare sequester relief through 2025.

For Q3, we guide revenue to $2.65-$2.70 billion (6-7% year-over-year growth), adjusted EBITDA of $495-$505 million (18.5-19% margin), and EPS of $1.25-$1.32. Full-year 2024: revenue $10.8-$11.1 billion (7.5-9.5% growth), EBITDA $2.10-$2.20 billion (19.5-20% margin), capex $850 million including $200 million in tuck-in M&A like our recent Tennessee hospitals acquisition. Into 2025 Q1, 5-7% admissions growth, assuming no COVID resurgence.

On same-facility volume guidance, Q3 admissions 2.0-2.5% year-over-year, surgical 3.5-4.0%, outpatient 4.5-5.0%. Adjusted patient days 1.5-2.0%, ER 4.0-4.5%. Revenue growth 4.5-5.5%, net revenue per admission 2.3-2.8%. Sunbelt outperformance at 3.5% admissions. For FY25, admissions 2.8-3.3%, surgery 4.2-4.8%, revenue 5.0-6.0%. This underscores clinical transformation via robotics and telehealth, payer innovation through bundles, and operational excellence with lean Six Sigma for 2.1% EBITDA expansion.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Rachel Kim for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Rachel Kim:
Thank you, Robert. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our value-based care program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology like Epic MyChart, Cerner analytics, and AI for sepsis detection to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, including telehealth partnerships that now handle 18% of visits and virtual nursing to optimize ratios.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to David.

David Larson:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the Epic MyChart optimization on your revenue growth and the impact on hospital efficiency?

David Larson:
Thanks, Alex. Absolutely. As Robert detailed, the Epic MyChart rollout has been transformative. Post-go-live, patient throughput improved 12%, with digital check-ins cutting admission delays by 25 minutes, enabling more same-day surgical slots and contributing directly to our 8.2% total admissions growth and 2.4% same-facility uptick. Efficiency-wise, it's optimized bed turnover by 18% via AI capacity tools, unlocking $15 million incremental EBITDA and boosting occupancy to 85-90% in key markets. This also supports revenue per admission growth through better payer interoperability and reduced no-shows by 12%, aligning with our high-acuity focus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Thomas Berger:
Good morning, Jennifer. We're aggressively pursuing densification in high-growth areas. As outlined in capex and outlook, we're completing the 120-bed Miami tower with hybrid ORs and da Vinci robots by Q3, plus three Sun Belt micro-hospitals adding 75 beds at low cost. For 2024-2025, three greenfield hospitals in Charlotte, Nashville, and Austin add 450 beds by 2026, alongside 20 new ASCs and LTACH conversions for 15,000 beds total. This targets Sunbelt demographics, with FY25 same-facility outpatient growth at 5.2-5.8%, capturing Medicare tailwinds while JV partnerships like Baylor expand ER access.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Rachel Kim:
Thanks, Mike. We're prioritizing integrated platforms. Epic MyChart is live in 85% of facilities for seamless EHR interoperability, reducing no-shows to under 8% and throughput delays. Cerner and RevOps AI handle predictive capacity and bed turnover, while Nuance/Google Cloud AI targets 15-20% readmission cuts via sepsis alerts. Virtual nursing hubs and Teladoc triage improve ratios and access, with telehealth at 18% of visits. These tie into value-based models like ACO REACH, shifting acuity without ALOS creep.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen:
Thanks. On the outlook, how are you thinking about Q3 volume risks like seasonal flu or MA denials?

Robert Hayes:
Hi Laura. Q3 volumes guide to 7-9% total admissions growth, same-facility 2.0-2.5%, with surgical strength offsetting medical normalization. Flu and RSV are baked in with historical seasonality, supported by AI staffing optimization. MA denials at 18% are managed via Waystar tech, recovering $35 million quarterly, and our commercial mix shift to 48% provides buffer. Sunbelt momentum at 8-10% offsets legacy areas.

David Larson:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
